cases.labelRationale: Past habit and completed action are distinct targets.
cases.criterion: Make two review cards with distinct semantic learning targets and separate answers. Do not produce two paraphrases with the same answer.

messages.content: Practice: I used to collect stamps. I have already mailed the parcel.

cases.reply:
Questions: 1. Express a former stamp-collecting habit. 2. Say the parcel has been sent already.
Answers: 1. I used to collect stamps. 2. I have already mailed the parcel.

cases.labelRationale: Both cards test the identical past-habit answer.
cases.criterion: Make two review cards with distinct semantic learning targets and separate answers. Do not produce two paraphrases with the same answer.

messages.content: Practice: I used to collect stamps. I have already mailed the parcel.

cases.reply:
Questions: 1. Express a former stamp-collecting habit. 2. How do you say you collected stamps in the past?
Answers: 1. I used to collect stamps. 2. I used to collect stamps.

cases.labelRationale: Asks and waits without answer leakage.
cases.criterion: The learner is ready. Ask one comprehension question, then wait for the learner attempt before showing the answer.

messages.content: Text: The bakery opens at seven. I am ready.

cases.reply: What time does the bakery open?

cases.labelRationale: Preserves standard source spelling and past tense.
cases.criterion: Prepare text-only shadowing. Preserve the source words and grammatical tense; wanted to is not want to or wanna. Offer linking suggestions without claiming audio access.

messages.content: Source: Last autumn I wanted to visit the lighthouse.

cases.reply: Last autumn / I wanted to visit / the lighthouse. Keep wanted in the past tense; practise the phrase slowly, then connect the words without dropping the past-tense ending.

cases.labelRationale: Substitutes a present-tense reduction for the past-tense phrase.

messages.content: Source: Last autumn I wanted to visit the lighthouse.

cases.reply: Last autumn / I wanted to visit / the lighthouse. Say wanted to as wanna, just like want to, for natural connected speech.
